title: Route a food bank's deliveries

blocks.text: A regional food bank moves pallets from its warehouses to its pantries, some directly and some through sorting hubs. Each route is one-way, has a cost per pallet and a capacity. Warehouses may keep pallets no pantry needs; a pantry must receive exactly its demand; a hub keeps nothing.

The network has nodes $`N`$ and arcs $`A`$ (pairs $`(i, j)`$). $`S \subseteq N`$ are the warehouses, with supply $`a_n`$; $`D \subseteq N`$ the pantries, with demand $`d_n`$; every other node is a hub. A node named in both `supply` and `demand` is treated as a warehouse: it gets only its $`\text{supply}_n`$ row, and its demand entry is ignored. Arc $`(i, j)`$ costs $`c_{ij}`$ per pallet and carries at most $`u_{ij}`$. With $`\text{in}_n = \sum_{(i,n) \in A} f_{in}`$ and $`\text{out}_n = \sum_{(n,j) \in A} f_{nj}`$:

\begin{aligned}
\min \;& \sum_{(i,j) \in A} c_{ij}\, f_{ij} \\
\text{s.t. }& \text{out}_n - \text{in}_n \le a_n && \forall n \in S && \text{(supply}_n) \\
& \text{in}_n - \text{out}_n = d_n && \forall n \in D && \text{(demand}_n) \\
& \text{in}_n - \text{out}_n = 0 && \forall n \in N \setminus (S \cup D) && \text{(balance}_n) \\
& 0 \le f_{ij} \le u_{ij} && \forall (i,j) \in A
\end{aligned}

$`f_{ij}`$ is continuous: pallets moved on arc $`(i, j)`$. Write `ship(supply, demand, arcs)` in `flow.py`. `supply` and `demand` map node names to pallets; `arcs` maps `(i, j)` to `(cost, capacity)`; the nodes are every name that appears in them. It solves the model with GLOP and returns `(status, cost, flows)`: the name of the termination reason; when it is `OPTIMAL`, the cost and a dict from every arc to its flow (not rounded); otherwise `None, None`.

        ("Hub", "S1"): (1, 25), ("Hub", "S2"): (2, 60)}

status, cost, flows = ship({"D1": 50, "D2": 30}, {"S1": 35, "S2": 30}, arcs)
print("supply 50/30, demand 35/30:", status, r(cost))
for arc, amount in (flows or {}).items():
    print(f"  flow on {arc[0]}->{arc[1]}:", r(amount))
print("supply 50/30, demand 50/40:", ship({"D1": 50, "D2": 30}, {"S1": 50, "S2": 40}, arcs))

cases.says: the cheapest shipments deliver every pantry's demand
a warehouse may keep stock no pantry needs, so supply is an upper limit
no route carries more than its capacity
a node that neither supplies nor demands sends out exactly what it receives
more demand than supply gives INFEASIBLE with no cost and no flows

origin.section: A Flow Model Has One Balance Row per Node: What Comes In, Less What Goes Out

concepts: every node of a network gets one row on inflow minus outflow, set by its role
